title: Counting with threads
description:
Count primes in parallel with C11 threads and an atomic counter.

```
4 threads, primes below 200000: 17984
with a plain int: wrong answers likely
with atomic_int: 17984 every time
```
hints: `int worker(void *arg) { int start = *(int *)arg; for (int n = start; n < 200000; n += 4) if (is_prime(n)) atomic_fetch_add(&count, 1); return 0; }` (lesson 7.05).
Give each thread its own `start` value in an array that lives until `thrd_join` returns.
requirements: Use `<threads.h>` (`thrd_create`, `thrd_join`); each thread checks every fourth number.
Show a version with a plain `int` and explain why it can lose updates.
If your C library has no `<threads.h>`, use `<pthread.h>` with the same structure.
stretch: Replace the atomic with a `mtx_t` and compare the time of both versions.
